subject: ENGLISH
title: More Than One · M01 D07
objective: Form regular plurals with -s or -es in taught examples.
introduction: Milo found one cat, then many cats! Help him add -s and -es to make plurals.

vocabulary.definition: A word that names a person, place, or thing.
The last letters of a word, like the -x in box or the -sh in dish.
More than one, like cats or boxes.

activities.instruction: Watch how nouns grow from one to many!
activities.content: Many nouns add -s; some nouns ending in s, x, z, sh, or ch add -es. Other nouns follow different patterns.

items.prompt: What is the plural of cat?
items.explanation: Cat just adds -s to mean more than one: one cat, two cats. Cates and caties add extra letters that are not part of the rule.

items.prompt: Which pair shows the plural made with -s?
items.explanation: Cat adds plain -s to become cats. Child and mouse are special words — childs and mouses are not correct plurals.
Child is a special word — its plural is children, not childs. Cats and boxes follow the -s and -es rules.

items.prompt: What is the plural of box?
items.explanation: Box ends with -x, so it takes -es: boxes. Boxs and boxen do not follow the rule.
Dish ends with -sh, so its plural is dishes. Foot and child change in a special way — their plurals are feet and children.
